summary: Tested new Audit Logs feature end-to-end. Backend: 12 pytest tests in /app/backend/tests/test_audit_logs.py all pass — login/CRUD (jobs)/team add-change-remove produce audit entries with fields {created_at,user_name,action}; date filter is honored server-side (today range returns today's entries, past-only and future-only ranges return []); CSV export returns Content-Type text/csv, Content-Disposition attachment, first line exactly 'Timestamp,User,Action', row count matches list endpoint, future-only range yields just the header row; RBAC — foreman gets 403 on both /api/audit-logs and /api/audit-logs/export, unauthenticated also blocked. Frontend Playwright: logged in as owner, nav-audit-logs opens /app/audit-logs which renders audit-logs-page with 13 audit-log-row entries; setting audit-start-date=2099-01-01 & audit-end-date=2099-01-02 + clicking audit-apply-filter-btn triggers GET /api/audit-logs?start=2099-01-01&end=2099-01-02 (200) and shows audit-empty state; audit-export-btn triggers GET /api/audit-logs/export?start=2099-01-01&end=2099-01-02 (200, text/csv). RBAC: freshly-created foreman logged in — sidebar has NO nav-audit-logs; navigating to /app/audit-logs redirects to /app; direct fetch of /api/audit-logs and /api/audit-logs/export returns 403. ONE FRONTEND BUG FOUND: audit-clear-filter-btn clears the input state but the table does NOT refresh with unfiltered data — it stays on the previous (empty) result set.

ui_bugs.issue: Clicking audit-clear-filter-btn empties the date inputs (start='' / end='') but the audit-logs table stays empty. Reproduces after any filter that returns 0 rows (e.g. 2099 range). Root cause: the Clear onClick does `setStart(''); setEnd(''); setTimeout(load, 0);`. Because `load` is memoized via useCallback([start, end]), the reference captured inside setTimeout is the PREVIOUS load closure (still holding start='2099-...',end='2099-...'). React hasn't re-rendered by the time the 0-ms timeout fires, so the stale load runs with the old params and returns []. The result: UI shows blank inputs but the still-empty table.

action_items: Fix AuditLogs.js Clear button so the table refreshes with unfiltered results. Recommended fix: replace `setTimeout(load, 0)` with an inline reload that does not depend on stale state, e.g. `setStart(''); setEnd(''); const {data}=await api.get('/audit-logs'); setLogs(data);` — OR — drive the reload from a useEffect that watches [start,end]: `useEffect(() => { load(); }, [load]);` (removing the current one-time useEffect) so any change to the date state (including clearing) auto-triggers a fresh fetch with the correct params.
critical_code_review_comments: Server-side date filter is correctly implemented via _audit_query building a Mongo query with $gte/$lte on the created_at ISO string field — filter IS applied in the DB query, not client-side. Verified via future-range returning [] both on list and export endpoints.
CSV export uses csv.writer (proper quoting) + StarletteResponse with text/csv + attachment Content-Disposition — headers exactly as specified.

log_audit is invoked from every required action in server.py (login line 210, crud create/update/delete lines 319/334/341, estimates create/send 368/423, timecards clock-in/out 459/474, team add/role-change/remove 626/649/659, data-entry ticket submit 687).
Both /api/audit-logs and /api/audit-logs/export use Depends(require_role('owner')) — RBAC verified (foreman -> 403).
Frontend Layout NAV correctly restricts Audit Logs to roles:['owner'] and App.js route uses Protected roles=['owner'] which redirects non-owners to /app.

MINOR: AuditLogs.js exports filename in client and backend independently; if we care about consistency the client should just honor the server's Content-Disposition filename instead of building its own.
MINOR: 1000-row limit on GET /api/audit-logs may silently truncate for large tenants without any UI indication. Consider pagination or an explicit 'showing latest 1000' hint.

rca of the issue: AuditLogs.js line 86: `onClick={() => { setStart(''); setEnd(''); setTimeout(load, 0); }}`. `load` is a useCallback memoized with deps [start, end]. At click time it's the closure with old start/end. React schedules re-render for setStart/setEnd but does NOT rebuild `load` synchronously; setTimeout(0) fires before the next render, invoking the STALE `load` which sends the previous (empty-result) params. Result: UI state cleared, network call & table still filtered. Fixes above.
